findings.title: Blocking search index build now in NewResourceServer constructor can cause long startup / deadlock risk
findings.body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously, which triggers searchSupport.init() that builds the full index for all namespaces before returning from the constructor. For large installations this can take a very long time, blocking server startup (and anything that constructs ResourceServer, e.g. module server wiring, tests, or other services that expect fast construction). Any caller relying on fast/non-blocking construction (previously relying on lazy init during the first gRPC call) will now be blocked indefinitely or until index build completes, with no timeout or context deadline applied to the Init call.

findings.title: Stop() mutates initErr without synchronization against Init()/once
findings.body: Stop() sets s.initErr directly outside of the sync.Once guarded path used by Init(). If Init() is still running concurrently (e.g., background watcher goroutine) while Stop() executes, there's a race writing/reading s.initErr without synchronization (no mutex, no atomic). This was already present before, but now that Init() runs synchronously at construction and the once can still fire later from other paths, the race window remains and reviewers should flag that initErr access is unguarded.

findings.title: totalBatchesIndexed increment and errgroup closure captures loop variable info unsafely in older style
findings.body: In the init loop, group.Go closures use the loop variable `info` from `for _, info := range stats`. Depending on Go version semantics (pre-1.22) and since the closures run concurrently, capturing `info` without taking a local copy inside the goroutine can lead to data races/incorrect namespace reported if Go version < 1.22. Also totalBatchesIndexed++ is incremented from multiple goroutines without synchronization (concurrent writes to the same int from errgroup goroutines), which is a data race since initWorkers can run several goroutines in parallel.

findings.title: NewResourceServer now returns error on index build failure, changing behavior/contract for existing callers
findings.body: Previously, failures in search index initialization (e.g., transient DB/network issues during index build) only affected the first gRPC call lazily. Now any error returned from s.search.init(ctx) during NewResourceServer causes construction of the ResourceServer to fail entirely, preventing the whole module/server from starting. This is a notable behavior change: any transient issue in index building (e.g., one misbehaving namespace or stats collection failure) will block the entire resource server from being created, with no partial-start fallback.
